metaTitle: SIT31021 Cert III in Patisserie RPL — Pastry Chef
metaDescription: Working as a pastry cook? Get the SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie through RPL using your kitchen experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie is the trade qualification for pastry cooks. If you already make cakes, pastries, desserts and yeast goods in a commercial kitchen, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Pastry cooks and commis pastry chefs
  • Bakers who specialise in cakes and pastries
  • Cooks who run the dessert section in restaurants or hotels
  • Pastry cooks who trained overseas

You'll usually have two or more years in a commercial kitchen producing cakes, pastries, petits fours, desserts and yeast-based products, while following food safety rules.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of products you've made: cakes, pastries, desserts, petits fours
  • Recipes, production plans and order sheets you've worked from
  • A reference from your head chef, head pastry chef or employer
  • Food safety and food handler certificates
  • Payslips or a statement of service showing your kitchen roles
description: The SIT31021 Certificate III in Patisserie covers the skills of a qualified pastry cook: producing cakes, specialised cakes, pastries, petits fours, desserts and yeast-based bakery products, using food preparation equipment, basic cookery methods, working effectively in a commercial kitchen, food safety and hygiene, stock control and coaching others.

faqs.q: Can I get a patisserie qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have worked as a pastry cook. Photos of your products, recipes and a chef's reference are assessed against the units, and practical skills are observed or recorded.
Usually 6 to 12 weeks, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: Do I need to do a practical assessment?
faqs.a: Usually yes. An assessor watches you produce a range of products in a commercial kitchen, or reviews recorded video, to confirm your skills.

faqs.q: I trained as a pastry chef overseas. Can my experience count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas experience and training can be assessed. Photos, references and any certificates help, and recent Australian kitchen work strengthens your evidence.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

Not automatically. The RSA is issued under your state's liquor rules. Tell us your state and we'll point you to the right course.
